question: Should the owner-ratified HITL escalation rule be amended with the review-convergence amendment -- a charter before round 1, a 2-round default review budget, narrowed escalation triggers, same-day escalation asks with defaults, recorded deadline defaults, caps for non-review loops, report-only tooling and paired metrics -- replacing the rule's "3 rounds" trigger? The structured question as asked is quoted verbatim in `decision`.
recommendation: The option the coordinator marked as recommended in the structured question: "Ratify as written (Recommended)".
decision:
The owner ratified this amendment in owner chat on 2026-09-23, as the answer to a structured question. The question, the owner's selected answer, and that option's own description are quoted below VERBATIM, followed by the ratified list the question refers to as "as listed above", also VERBATIM. Nothing inside the quoted blocks is reworded; everything outside them is this record's own framing, not ratified text.

Question, verbatim:

> Ratify the review-convergence amendment to the HITL rule as listed above (charter with non-removable clauses, 2-round default budget, fresh final reviewer kept, triggers only for exhausted budget/stall/value dispute, same-day escalation asks with reversible defaults, deadline defaults recorded as decidedBy: default, caps for non-review loops, report-only tooling, paired metrics)? Only you can change the rule. Your answer is recorded verbatim from this chat, and the amendment lands as its own chartered PR.

Owner's selected answer, verbatim:

> Ratify as written (Recommended)

The selected option's description, verbatim:

> Recorded as an owner-chat decision. I open one chartered PR amending docs/HITL.md with a superseding decision record, and apply the budget to live work immediately, starting with #1354.

The ratified list ("as listed above"), verbatim:

> 1. **Charter before round 1.** Required for gate, governance, security or release paths, or over about 300 lines across the stack. It states the goal, adversary, non-goals, what "done" means, the blocking bar and the round budget. Five clauses are always on and can't be removed: harm, authority or permission effects, false claims, rule fidelity, and correctness. Reviewers first review the charter itself; they can add clauses, never remove them, and a charter defect blocks.
> 2. **Structured findings.** Each blocking finding cites a charter clause. The reviewer, not the author, labels it a new class or a known class, and a known class must cite its earlier instance. A finding with no clause becomes an issue.
> 3. **Budget.**
>    - The default is 2 rounds. A charter can ask for more, and that request is approved with the charter.
>    - In round 2, the same reviewers check their own findings, and one fresh strong-class final reviewer joins, as your rule requires. New findings block only under the always-on clauses.
>    - One automatic extra round is allowed only when blockers strictly shrink and every blocker is a new harm-class finding. Otherwise the PR goes to you.
> 4. **Triggers.** An item goes to you when any of these happens:
>    - the budget is exhausted;
>    - the review-run cap is hit;
>    - it stalls, with no progress since the last push, CI and queue time excluded;
>    - there's a value dispute.
>
>    Reviewer disagreement doesn't go to you. The stricter view wins, as your rule already says. A repeat of a known class makes me close that class by design, or document it as residual risk; it doesn't reach you either.
> 5. **Escalation packet.** One question, with options, my recommendation, a default and a deadline. It's asked same-day, at most twice a day, with related items merged.
>    - **Default for ordinary PRs:** park it and ship the parts that have converged.
>    - **Authority or governance PRs:** park the whole PR, never a partial landing.
>    - **Live-harm fixes:** ship the smallest fix and file the rest.
> 6. **Records.** Your answers, budget grants and deadline defaults are all recorded. A deadline default is recorded as `decidedBy: default`, so it can never count as your authority.
> 7. **Beyond reviews.** CI reruns, rebase churn and queue ejections get their own caps. A clean mechanical rebase, verified by a range-diff, keeps its review clearance.
> 8. **Tooling.** `review-loop-status` starts report-only, with its own charter. A quote-fidelity test checks that quoted rule text is word for word, and that reviewers receive the rule and charter verbatim.
> 9. **Metrics.** Reviewed at the Friday cut:
>    - rounds to converge;
>    - escalations;
>    - your decision latency;
>    - agent runs per merged PR;
>    - escaped defects;
>    - park rate.
>
>    Pairing speed with escaped defects keeps the speed targets from pushing reviewers to approve.

Effect on the ratified escalation rule (governance/decisions/hitl-escalation-rule.json), stated here as this record's own framing, not as ratified text: this amendment amends and supersedes the relevant parts of that rule. The rule's "3 rounds" escalation trigger -- Accepted item 5's "or after 3 rounds that go nowhere" and the "Your approval first" table row's "or 3 rounds that go nowhere" -- becomes the budget in item 3 of the list above, with the triggers in item 4. Where the rule's "Your approval first" row says an ask is "batched for Friday unless urgent", item 5 of the list above ("It's asked same-day, at most twice a day, with related items merged.") governs instead. Every other part of the ratified escalation rule stands unchanged, including its value-disagreement trigger, the stricter-view rule for reviewer disagreement, the fresh strong-class final reviewer, and "Changing this rule itself". The earlier record is not edited, since decided records are immutable; it stays in force except for the parts named above.
notes:
channel: owner-chat, not independently verifiable -- the same disclosure the ratified escalation rule requires of every owner-chat record (its "Where I'm pushing back" section says records of the owner's decisions cite this chat and are marked "chat channel, not independently verifiable"). The question, answer and option description were relayed to the drafting session by the coordinator, verbatim, from the owner chat; this record reproduces them as relayed.

Context the owner saw alongside the list, stated here in this record's own words and not quoted: the amendment followed a red-team whose recommendations were adopted, with one exception -- escalation asks go same-day instead of being batched to Friday.

Options: only the selected option's label and description were relayed to the drafting session, so `options` names that one option. Any other options the structured question offered are not reproduced here, rather than reconstructed from memory.

No `reviews[]` entries, for the same reason governance/decisions/hitl-escalation-rule.json gives: this is a ratification the owner made directly in chat, and the red-team that preceded it has no citable, durable link an entry here could point to (docs/contracts/decision-record.json: `reviews` may be empty for a `decidedBy: "owner"` record made without a prior agent recommendation).

`supersedes` is empty on purpose. In docs/contracts/decision-record.json, and in scripts/land-stack.mjs's evaluateTier2Decision, an id named in `supersedes` is treated as replaced as a whole. This amendment supersedes only the parts of hitl-escalation-rule named in `decision` above, so naming that id would claim the whole rule was replaced. The partial supersession is stated in `decision` instead.

`relaxesGateOrPolicy` is false: in net this is a new policy (charter, budget, triggers, escalation packet, records, caps, metrics), the contract's own example of a `false` record, and no gate or check in this repository changes with it -- the pull request that lands this record changes documentation only. Reviewers should check this call, because some individual items could read as loosening when a later change implements them: item 3 limits which new round-2 findings block, item 4 lets a repeated known class be documented as residual risk without reaching the owner, and item 7 keeps review clearance across a clean mechanical rebase. A later pull request that implements any of those in a gate must declare its own `relaxesGateOrPolicy` for that gate change; this record does not pre-declare it.

Known gap, not fixed here: item 6's `decidedBy: default` is not yet an accepted value in scripts/check-decision-records.mjs (DECIDED_BY_VALUES is owner and consensus), so a deadline default cannot yet be recorded in governance/decisions/ in the form item 6 names. Building that is follow-up work, like the review-loop-status script and the quote-fidelity test named in item 8.
